memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine follow‑up for coronary artery disease and irritable bowel syndrome.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional mild chest discomfort on exertion, relieved by rest, and intermittent bloating with loose stools twice weekly.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, pulse 78/min, weight 68 kg, height 158 cm, BMI 27.2 (obese). Cardiovascular examination is regular without murmurs. Abdomen is soft, non‑tender, no masses.
IMPRESSION: Stable CAD on current meds; IBS with mixed pattern. Lipids and glucose to be checked.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue aspirin 75 mg OD, atorvastatin 40 mg HS, metoprolol 25 mg OD, isosorbide mononitrate 20 mg OD, GTN SOS. For IBS: mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA. Advise low‑salt diet, 150 min/week brisk walking, weight target <63 kg. Return if chest pain at rest, breathlessness >20 min, fever >39°C, rectal bleeding, or worsening abdominal pain.

memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Cholesterol 190 mg/dL (<200), Triglycerides 140 mg/dL (<150), HDL 48 mg/dL (>40), LDL 112 mg/dL (<100 borderline high). Fasting blood sugar 98 mg/dL (70‑99). CBC: Hb 12.8 g/dL (12‑16), WBC 6.2 x10^9/L (4‑10), Platelets 210 x10^9/L (150‑400). Stool routine: Ova nil, pus cells 0‑1/hpf. tTG‑IgA: Negative (<7 U/mL).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Resting ECG: Sinus rhythm, rate 72/min. No ST‑segment depression or elevation. No pathological Q waves. Mild left ventricular voltage within normal limits. No arrhythmias.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up after lipid results and symptom review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She notes reduced exertional chest discomfort (once weekly) and improved bowel pattern (soft stools once daily). No new symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/80 mmHg, pulse 76/min, weight 66.5 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Cardiovascular regular. Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: LDL remains above target; consider intensifying statin. IBS controlled. Advise weight reduction.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase atorvastatin to 40 mg HS (continue). Add ezetimibe 10 mg OD if LDL >100 after 4 weeks. Continue other CAD meds. IBS regimen unchanged. Repeat lipid profile in 8 weeks. Return if chest pain at rest, palpitations, fainting, severe abdominal pain, or bloody stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Exercise treadmill test (Bruce protocol): She reached stage 3 (3 METs) before limiting fatigue. No ST‑segment depression >1 mm. No arrhythmia. Blood pressure rose appropriately to 160/90 mmHg at peak. Test interpreted as negative for inducible ischemia.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Six‑month review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional mild epigastric discomfort after meals, no chest pain. Bowels regular.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, pulse 74/min, weight 65 kg, BMI 26.0 (overweight). Cardiovascular regular. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in left lower quadrant, no guarding.
IMPRESSION: LDL at goal. IBS symptoms mild, likely diet‑related. No cardiac ischemia on recent treadmill.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue aspirin 75 mg OD, atorvastatin 40 mg HS, ezetimibe 10 mg OD, metoprolol 25 mg OD, isosorbide mononitrate 20 mg OD, GTN SOS. IBS: mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Advise low‑fat diet, avoid trigger foods, maintain activity. Repeat lipid profile and fasting sugar in 4 months. Return if chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, syncope, worsening abdominal pain, vomiting, or rectal bleeding.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram: Left ventricular end‑diastolic diameter 4.8 cm (normal). Left ventricular ejection fraction 60% (normal). Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. No valvular stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. No regional wall motion abnormality.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Winter check‑up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional mild frontal headache and sensation of light‑headedness on standing, especially after morning walk. No chest pain. Bowels normal.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/70 mmHg (lower than usual), pulse 72/min, weight 64.2 kg, BMI 25.6 (overweight). Cardiovascular regular. Abdomen soft, non‑tender.
IMPRESSION: Orthostatic hypotension possibly related to isosorbide mononitrate in setting of lower BP. LDL well controlled.
ARRANGEMENTS: Discontinue isosorbide mononitrate. Continue aspirin 75 mg OD, atorvastatin 40 mg HS, ezetimibe 10 mg OD, metoprolol 25 mg OD, GTN SOS. Advise rise slowly from sitting/standing, adequate hydration, salt modest increase if symptomatic. IBS meds unchanged. Repeat BP in 2 weeks, lipid profile in 3 months. Return if chest pain, palpitations, fainting, fall, worsening headache, or abdominal pain with vomiting.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review after BP monitoring.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She denies dizziness since stopping isosorbide; occasional mild shoulder discomfort after lifting groceries, non‑cardiac. Bowels regular.
EXAMINATION: BP 124/76 mmHg, pulse 76/min, weight 63.8 kg, BMI 25.5 (overweight). Cardiovascular regular. Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Orthostatic symptoms resolved. LDL remains at target. No new cardiac symptoms.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue aspirin 75 mg OD, atorvastatin 40 mg HS, ezetimibe 10 mg OD, metoprolol 25 mg OD, GTN SOS. IBS regimen unchanged. Encourage strength training twice weekly, maintain weight <63 kg. Repeat lipid profile and fasting sugar in 6 months. Return if chest pain, exertional dyspnea, palpitations, syncope, abdominal pain with vomiting or bleeding, or new neurologic symptoms.
